title: Not wanting to be a nursemaid to the band
summary: Bad sight and a broken hip made him need help crossing streets, and he did not want bandmates to babysit him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well in these past three years, since you've been having trouble with your eyes, does that mean you haven't worked very much?

Well, no, not too much. Not too much, because I don't like being out, this and that, where I can't see, and you've got to have somebody help you cross here, help you do this, even on my European thing there, with Red, they helped me to clear there, because I couldn't see too well, and I don't walk too well because of my broken hip,
you know, and the built-up shoe, and a walking cane, and all that thing.
So, when you start to think about it, the buy offers you a job, you say man, nobody wants to be a babysitter, you know, nursemaid to a guy. Shoot! That's too much!

And I appreciate what Red did, and the drummer, George Reed, and all the guys in the band, they were always willing, but after all, how much can the guys -- you know. I don't care if it's your own brother, your own father. I mean you can get tired of it sometimes (laughs) you know.
